PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  ACTION SUMMARY
  March 21, 2023, COMMISSION MEETING

Commission Members Present: Larry Giannone (Chair), Albert Behr, Bob Olander, Edward
Rodriguez, Karol Curtis, Morgan Kostolefsky, Patrick Jones, Tim Hughes
Commission Members Absent:
City Representatives: City Council Liaison Ryan Vienna, City Manager Chris Constantin,
Captain Walid Ashrafnia
 ORAL COMMUNICATIONS  COMMENTS/RECOMMENDATIONS
  Cathi Began thanked the Los Angeles Sheriffs
  Department for their extra patrol in the Calle
  Cristina area.

  Sean Cazares thanked the City for considering
  support for AB23. He highlighted that there are
  2,500 bills currently in the legislature with
  significant implications. In one bill that passed
  the Assembly public safety committee, the bill
  would ban police from using K9s to apprehend
  individuals during crowd control situations.

 BUSINESS ITEMS  COMMENTS/RECOMMENDATIONS
 3.1 Approval of the January 17, 2023 Meeting  Motion by Kostolefsky/Seconded by Curtis to
 Minutes  approve minutes of January 17, 2023. (Passed
  8-0).

 3.2 2023 Year Crime Statistics and Trends  Captain Ashrafnia updated the commission on
 (Captain Walid Ashrafnia)  the 2023 crime statistics and trends. Overall,
  crime was up by 2% from 2022. Specifically,
  the area of concern was petty thefts which were
  up. Assaults, robberies, and burglaries were
  down.
 March 21, 2023 Public Safety Commission Minutes  Page 2

  There was a reported sexual assault at
  Horsethief Canyon trails. A be on the lookout
  was issued, and San Dimas station personnel
  were working to identify and apprehend the
  individual.

  Deputies performed a crosswalk operation
  downtown on Bonita. The purpose of the
  operation was to improve safety downtown for
  pedestrians. The operation resulted in the
  issuance of 20 citations in the first hour.

 3.3 Discussion of CERT Status and Training  Larry Giannone, the City’s volunteer
 (Larry Giannone)  coordinator, reported that the current cohort of
  CERT members were going to complete
  training in April. The final exercise would be
  April 20th. He expects a new cohort to be
  prepared by the end of the year.

 3.4 Discussion regarding recommending to the  City Manager Constantin reported on the status
 City Council Support for Assembly Bill 23 by  of the bill and recommended the commission
 Assemblymember Muratshuchi: Theft:  take a watch position. The commission
 shoplifting: amount (City Manager Chris  concurred with this direction.
 Constantin)

 REPORTS  COMMENTS/RECOMMENDATIONS
 Commissioner Reports  Commissioners provided updates.

 City Council Liaison  City Council Liaison Ryan Vienna reported
  that theft in some cities is a public nuisance
  when the business does not desire prosecution
  but results in significant police response. This
  was intended to avoid the waste of public
  resources.

  The City Council was making changes to the
  board and commission handbook in the areas of
  membership, terms, and size of the
  commission. The City Council would evaluate
  input it received during a special meeting
  related to these areas.

 City Staff Liaison  City Manager Chris Constantin discussed the
  essence of the proposed changes to the City’s
  Boards and Commission Handbook. He also
 March 21, 2023 Public Safety Commission Minutes  Page 3

  advised the commission on the date of the next
  business watch meeting.

  Constantin updated the commission on the
  storm damaged incurred during the recent rain
  and wind event.

The meeting adjourned at 7:12 PM.
   PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  ACTION SUMMARY
  May 21, 2024, COMMISSION MEETING

Commission Members Present: Larry Giannone (Chair), Patrick Jones, Orlando Pimental, Greg
Tober, Ruth Luevand
Commission Members Absent: Bob Olander, Karol Curtis
City Representatives: City Manager Chris Constantin, Captain Walid Ashrafnia, Lieutenant
Luis Serrano, Sergeant James Hubbard
  •  Motion by Pimental, seconded by Jones to excuse the absence of Commissioner Bob
  Olander due to his public service work providing grants to students at San Dimas High
  School.
 ORAL COMMUNICATIONS  COMMENTS/RECOMMENDATIONS
  None

 BUSINESS ITEMS  COMMENTS/RECOMMENDATIONS
 BI.1 Approval of Minutes for March 19, 2024  Motion by Patrick Jones and seconded by
 (City Manager Chris Constantin)  Orlando Pimental to approve the minutes of
  March 19, 2024. (Passed 5-0).

 BI.2 Discussion of Part 1 Crimes for January  Captain Ashrafnia provided an update on part 1
 to March 2024 Compared with 2023 (Captain  crime statistics for January to March 2024 as
 Walid Ashrafnia)  compared the same period in 2023. Total Part
  1 crime was up 2%. Assaults were down,
  violent crime was down, burglaries were down.
  Robberies were up by 2, auto theft was up, and
  there has been an uptick in graffiti both San
  Dimas and La Verne.
 May 21, 2024 Public Safety Commission Minutes  Page 2

 NEW BUSINESS  COMMENTS/RECOMMENDATIONS

 NB.1 Discussion of A New $200,000 Public  City Manager Constantin updated the
 Safety Grant Provided by the San Gabriel  Commission on the new grant that San Dimas
 Valley Council of Governments (City Manager  would receive from the San Gabriel Valley
 Chris Constantin)  Council of Governments.

  The grant would provide $200,000 for public
  safety related expenses. The scope was broad
  and could include the purchases of drones for
  City use, cameras to combat crime in high
  crime areas, and other technology.
 REPORTS  COMMENTS
 R1 Commissioner Reports  Larry Giannone – Recommended that Public
  Works review signal phasing outside of
  Starbucks at Arrow Highway near Inhouse
  Coffee.

  Ruth Luevand – Discussed safety on the Metro
  line and discussed the need for extra patrols on
  the A line when it becomes operative.

  Orlando Pimental – Discussed using the public
  safety grant to support homeless efforts.
  Additionally, downtown is in need of
  resurfacing.

  Patrick Jones – Asked who would respond to a
  call for service at the A line platform.
 R2 Station Captain’s Report (Captain
 Ashrafnia)  None.

 R3 City Staff Liaison Report (City Manager
 Chris Constantin)  City Manager Constantin confirmed who was
  attending the San Dimas dam tour.

The meeting adjourned at 6:21 PM.
